key_insight: OPCD trains a student language model on its own generated (on-policy) trajectories and aligns it to a context-conditioned teacher by minimizing reverse KL, letting the model internalize in‑context knowledge into its parameters.
problem_solved: How to reliably distill contextual (in‑context) behavior into model weights without relying solely on teacher-generated trajectories or off‑policy mismatch—so models can retain and use example-driven knowledge from their parameters.
method: On‑policy data collection: student model generates its own context-conditioned trajectories.
Alignment objective: minimize reverse Kullback–Leibler divergence between the student's trajectory distribution and a context‑conditioned teacher.
Parameter update: train the student to internalize contextual patterns so fewer or shorter external prompts are needed at inference.
impact: Enables language models to absorb example-based behaviors into weights, improving robustness and reducing dependence on long prompting—useful for deployment efficiency, personalization, and tasks requiring experiential knowledge.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: context → student generates trajectories → compute reverse KL vs context-conditioned teacher → update student weights
Two‑distribution schematic: overlapping probability curves illustrating reverse KL minimization (student → teacher alignment)
Before/after bar chart: performance or prompt‑length required pre‑ and post‑OPCD
Icon set: prompt → brain/weights (internalization), shield (robustness), speedometer (efficiency)
paper_title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
paper_authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei
